_comment: UPSTREAM TOOL INVENTORY for charmbracelet/crush. This file is a DRIFT TRIPWIRE, not configuration: tests/test_tool_inventory.py asserts every name here classifies to the stated class under the gate's VOCAB, and that none of them classify as 'unknown'. A shared lib cannot catch a tool the adapter never heard of - that is how web_fetch, web_search, sourcegraph, read_mcp_resource and list_mcp_resources ended up registered upstream and swept by nothing (CBP review, thread harness-lane-split, 2026-07-24). When upstream adds a tool, add it here with an explicit class; until then the gate treats it as UNKNOWN and gates it hardest, so the failure mode is over-block rather than a silent exfil channel.
_provenance: Names carrying a source reference are source-verified against charmbracelet/crush@main. Names without one are from the adapter's original documented-tier survey and are NOT source-verified - they are listed so their class is at least explicit. Live confirmation belongs on an onboarding rig with a real crush install.
_classes: read = local read, may skip Gate-2 | write = mutates local files | exec = runs a command | egress = touches the network | mcp = MCP-family, argument shape is the server's

tools.name: lsp_rename
tools.note: MUTATES source despite the lsp_ reader prefix (CBP CRUSH-4)

tools.name: lsp_replace_symbol
tools.note: MUTATES source despite the lsp_ reader prefix (CBP CRUSH-4)

tools.name: read_mcp_resource
tools.note: MCP-family but the name starts read_, so a bare mcp-prefix sweep missed it (CBP CRUSH-2)

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.note: MCP-family but the name starts list_, so a bare mcp-prefix sweep missed it (CBP CRUSH-2)

_mcp_naming: Dynamic MCP tools are built as mcp_<server>_<tool> (SINGLE underscore) at internal/agent/tools/mcp-tools.go:59, NOT the Claude mcp__<server>__<tool>. gate_core.normalize_mcp_name() translates at the governor boundary (CBP CRUSH-3).
